title: The babaylan asks for an offering
story: Sickness lingers in the barangay. The babaylan says the anito must be fed: a pig, rice and wine set out at the hut, with chants through the night.

choices.label: Hold the full rite
choices.result: The chanting lasts until dawn. In the days after, the sick rise from their mats.

choices.label: A small offering
choices.result: A little rice is set out at the hut. One of the sick feels better by morning.

choices.label: Wait and see
choices.result: The babaylan bows and returns to the hut. The sick must mend on their own.

_note: Babaylan (Visayan) and catalonan (Tagalog) were ritual specialists, very often women, who led healing rites with offerings to the anito.
sources: William Henry Scott, Barangay: Sixteenth-Century Philippine Culture and Society (Ateneo de Manila University Press, 1994), chapters on Visayan and Tagalog religion
Juan de Plasencia, Customs of the Tagalogs (1589), in Blair and Robertson, The Philippine Islands 1493–1898, vol. 7
